title: Investigate and mitigate stream ACK mismatch causing tenant-level stall and partial outputs
creator: Maya Greene
description: Several customers reported truncated server-sent event (SSE) streams where final segments never arrive. Root cause appears to be an ACK-sequence mismatch between the public gateway and the per-tenant runtime proxy which causes the gateway to classify a session as stalled and forcibly tear down the connection mid-output, leading to partial outputs and customer escalations. This ticket coordinates triage, a short-term mitigation patch, and the longer-term protocol hardening and SDK reconciliation flow.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create a long-running streaming generation request via hosted API (tenant with high concurrent sessions).
2) Simulate intermittent packet reorder between gateway and runtime (introduce 50-200ms jitter) or enable per-tenant rate-limiter spike,
3) Observe gateway ACK counter increment out-of-sync with runtime checkpoint messages,
4) Gateway marks session as stalled after missing expected ACK window and issues connection close,
5) Client receives truncated SSE stream without terminal event or final logits chunk.
observed_telemetry: Increase in gateway.SessionCloseReason=StallMark for specific tenant IDs (correlation: corr-20250128-xyz),
Runtime emitted checkpoint events at offsets 120, 240 but gateway expected 121, 241 due to an off-by-one on gateway ACK re-assembly code,
Spike in 499/408 client disconnects reported from the SDK in the 14:00-16:00 UTC window,
Affected tenants primarily on Hosted but also observed in Dedicated when tenant-specific proxy optimization is enabled.
initial_mitigation: Rollback gateway ACK-aggregation optimization (hotfix deployed to staging 2025-01-30). Temporarily increase stall detection window from 2s to 8s for affected tenants via runtime config flag to reduce false-positive stalls. Provide customers with SDK patch 0.9.12 that will attempt transparent resume with sequence reconciliation.
root_cause_summary: A combination of aggressive ACK aggregation in the public gateway and an off-by-one in the gateway's reassembly logic created an ACK sequence drift against the runtime's checkpoint stream. The drift was amplified under jitter/rate-limiter bursts so the gateway's stall heuristic fired prematurely. The client SDK lacked a robust resume-and-merge path for these edge cases, making truncated outputs visible to end users.
hotfix_plan: A) Immediate: Disable ACK aggregation optimization in gateway across all regions (done 2025-01-30),
B) Short-term: Patch gateway reassembly to tolerate out-of-order ACKs and re-sync using runtime checkpoints (PR #4842),
C) Short-term: Add gateway telemetry tag to mark 'soft-stall' vs 'hard-stall' and only hard-close on repeated confirmation,
D) Medium-term: Add explicit checkpoint marker events to protocol (runtime + SDK + gateway contract).
E) Long-term: Add per-tenant adaptive stall thresholds tied to workload shape and observed RTT distribution.
customer_communication: 2025-01-29: Notified customers A, C, and D with temporary mitigation steps and committed ETA for soft-fix (48h).
2025-02-02: Sent follow-up noting hotfix rollout to staging and shortly to prod; offered plan for additional retries via SDK patch.
Apology + Postmortem promised in 72 hours after final validation.
engineer_notes: Rajan: Reproduced locally using packet jitter harness and confirmed off-by-one in gateway seq merge (fix branch: fix/ack-reassembly-882).
Priya (SRE): Increased stall window for 3 tenants and saw no further truncated streams in Canary for 36h.
Edge case: Dedicated nodes with proxy-accelerator enabled still showed occasional drift — will add regression test to infra suite.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Relaxing stall detection trades increased time-to-detect genuine stalls for fewer false-positive disconnects. Longer stall windows may increase latency for real failures but reduce client-visible truncations. Checkpoint events increase protocol overhead slightly but improve determinism.
next_steps: 1) Merge and deploy gateway reassembly patch to canary (owner: Rajan) target 2025-02-11,
2) Validate canary with synthetic jitter scenarios across Hosted and Dedicated (owner: SRE),
3) Release SDK 0.9.12 with resume-and-merge logic to opt-in customers (owner: DX team) target 2025-02-14,
4) Draft protocol change RFC for explicit checkpoint markers and rollout plan across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (owner: Platform),
5) Prepare customer-facing postmortem and internal runbook for similar incidents.
postmortem_actions: Add unit/regression tests for ACK reassembly and out-of-order toleration,
Instrument per-tenant stall-window histograms and alert on sudden window shrinkage,
Create an SDK resume test harness and run during pre-release,
Document recommended tenant configurations for Dedicated (proxy-accelerator: off by default until compatibility verified).
resolution_criteria: No new truncated-stream customer escalations for affected tenants for 7 days post full fix; canary shows <0.1% soft-stall false positives under synthetic jitter at production QPS; SDK resume flow validated by DX tests.
final_notes: This ticket focuses on gating the immediate production pain through a small gateway patch and SDK opt-in resume support. Protocol-level changes will be tracked in a follow-on RFC to ensure durable correctness across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
